entries.current_evidence: Metadata table updates with schema rewrite jobs apply atomically, schema progress waits for hosting nodes, schema rewrite workers invalidate stale range jobs before rewriting rows, and table-emptying barriers validate complete ready range jobs before data-generation or restart-identity promotion.
entries.missing_evidence: Concurrent-reader/writer tests still need to drive live rewrite, table-emptying, CAS promotion, restart-identity reset, and reopen paths together and prove no operation observes or writes mixed schema generations.
entries.evidence_symbol: metadata raft apply store applies table updates with schema rewrite jobs atomically

entries.current_evidence: Applied SQL DDL supports CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE catalog application, marks rebuild/validation/rewrite work, deterministically schedules typed, row-plan, and full-row schema rewrite jobs from applied DDL work, persists table updates with rewrite jobs atomically across metadata reopen, and promotes completed rewrite work through table schema CAS.
entries.missing_evidence: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE still needs one durable schema-job workflow that owns validation, rewrite/backfill admission, CAS promotion, retry/abort decisions, reopen replay, and idempotent convergence. Existing catalog-apply and rewrite-job pieces are release evidence only after a single recoverable workflow ties them together.
entries.evidence_symbol: catalog jobs schedules full row schema rewrite jobs from applied SQL DDL work

entries.current_evidence: SQL DROP TABLE CASCADE updates child schemas and records catalog work items, while the table-emptying barrier machinery independently schedules cascade-aware multi-table jobs, repairs jobs after range topology changes, waits for every affected table range, resets identity allocators, promotes data generations, and removes completed durable jobs.
entries.missing_evidence: DROP TABLE CASCADE still needs one recoverable multi-table schema job that combines child schema updates with table-emptying/range cleanup, sequence cleanup, partial-progress recovery, reopen replay, and idempotent restart convergence. Existing child-schema cleanup and table-emptying barriers are separate release-gated pieces until that job owns the full cascade.
entries.evidence_symbol: metadata catalog validation applies sql drop table cascade through child schema updates

entries.current_evidence: Schema rewrite and table-emptying jobs expose durable lifecycle operations, progress records, stale lease rejection/takeover through lease expiry, wake loops, busy-only worker passes, invalidation with last_error, HTTP worker routes, admin-snapshot job visibility, and typed metadata manager/service/catalog-source controls for pause, resume, retry/requeue, and cancel. Raft transition commands persist those operator controls across reopen for both job families, and internal metadata HTTP routes expose all eight controls with deterministic 404/405/409 response classes. Worker passes now share an explicit admission policy for lease TTL, per-pass work bounds, and stale-running-job admission; focused coverage proves both job families honor the bounds and can disable or allow stale lease takeover admission.
entries.evidence_symbol: schema job worker admission policy bounds work and stale takeover; metadata raft apply store persists schema and table emptying operator controls across reopen
